M1.reason: The outline reads as a figure that stands fairly upright in the left and right views, with only a slight forward lean of the torso (sides.png LEFT and RIGHT, walk frames 0 to 23). The hunch the brief asks for is mild. The head is a smooth pink dome sitting on the shoulders, so the parasite does not show as its own shape in the silhouette. Arms reaching forward and the torn coat hem do match the brief.

M2.reason: Measured size 37.4 x 35.4 x 68.7 against the 68 asked: height is 0.01 off, and the length and width are within the 15% band of a brief's size.

M3.reason: Named parts are all there: the parasite dome over the head with a dark jaw (sides FRONT, LEFT), the lab coat, legs and boots, and long clawed hands on both arms (white claws at FRONT right hand, BACK left, RIGHT hand). The claws are short and their count does not read clearly at this size, but they are present on both hands and are not charged as missing.

M4.reason: The coat is white to grey with red-brown blood on its lower front and back (sides.png FRONT, BACK). The hands are dark brown-red, and the head is pink-red skin. Each region's colour fits what the brief asks: a white coat, bloodied, and skin.

M5.reason: The coat's tears and jagged hem, the blood smears, and the front buttons are there in their places (sides.png FRONT, FRONT-LEFT, BACK-RIGHT). The sharpness is consistent across the views, and nothing is smeared beyond what the brief asks for.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test: in the four readings of lineup.png the judges did not pick the asset as the one not made by Valve (they picked D, B, A, D where the asset was B, D, D, B).

M7.reason: The front is clearly the front: the face, mouth and coat buttons face the front view. The figure stands upright on its feet in every view, with its origin at the floor.

M8.reason: checkErrors is empty. Triangles are 692, under the 1008 limit (twice the median of 504 is larger than the third quartile of 731). In the below and top views the underside is closed with no visible openings, and the claws and coat stay attached in every view.

C1.reason: Walk frames 0 to 23 and attack frames 0 to 7: the hands, arms, coat, head and legs stay on the body through the walk cycle and the reach. Nothing comes apart, sinks or floats. The attack motion is small and mostly in the arms, so it shows little of the slash the brief describes, but no part leaves the body.
